title: Draw a family tree and add one story per person
description: A family tree of bare names is a diagram. Add one true story to every name — the day they met, the job they loved, the meal they were famous for — and it becomes the family itself.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Draw the branches
paragraphs: Start with the youngest generation at the bottom and work upward: parents, grandparents, great-grandparents as far as anyone can remember. Big paper helps, and pencil is wiser than pen — every family tree gets corrected by an aunt.
Where knowledge runs out, leave a named gap rather than guessing. A gap is an honest question mark, and it often sends someone to phone a relative — which is where the best stories come from anyway.

body.heading: One story each
paragraphs: Now the real work: for every name, add one story in a single line. Not 'was nice' — a story: crossed the sea with one suitcase, kept bees, won the argument with the mayor. Ask the oldest relatives first; their lines are the ones that cannot be re-asked later.
Date the tree and keep it somewhere safe. Next year's version will be longer, and the children who watched you draw it will one day be the ones correcting it.

takeaway: Draw the tree in pencil, leave honest gaps, and give every name one true story — starting with the oldest relatives, whose stories cannot be re-asked later.
materials: A phone to call relatives for stories (optional)
supervision: An adult should lead the calls to relatives and check family details before anything is shared beyond the family.
safetyNotes: Keep the finished tree private within the family — it contains personal information.
Be gentle with gaps: adoption, loss and family rifts deserve care, not interrogation.
